title: How fast is a ride of one hundred and twenty six kilometres?
description: A scooter ride of one hundred and twenty six kilometres takes two point five hours. The time is written as twenty five over ten, so the division becomes one thousand two hundred and sixty over twenty five, and a long division finishes it. Keeko's doubt is that only the divisor needs changing.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the divisor is changed into a counting number, the number being divided is changed by the same amount. Watch for students who change only the divisor.

source: {{NAME_9}} rides 126 km from Pune to Matheran in 2.5 hours. What is the average speed?
video_script.why: The child can divide by a counting number but changes only the divisor when it is a decimal.
video_script.substitution: Two point five is twenty five over ten, so dividing by it is multiplying by ten over twenty five.
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_9}} rides a hundred and twenty six kilometres from Pune to Matheran in two point five hours
video_script.wrong_answer: five point zero four kilometres per hour
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko changes two point five into twenty five but leaves a hundred and twenty six as it is.
video_script.payoff_line: The average speed is fifty point four kilometres per hour.

final_answer.spoken: fifty point four kilometres per hour

video_script.fraction_reading: A fraction such as 25/10 is read twenty five over ten, 10/25 is ten over twenty five, and 1260/25 is one thousand two hundred and sixty over twenty five.
maths_rules: the slip: 126 / 25 = 5.04, and 5.04 x 2.5 = 12.6, far short of 126
video_script.design: The ride stays on the board; the time becomes a fraction, the division becomes a counting-number division, and a long division finishes it.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a road from Pune to Matheran marked 126 km, with a clock reading 2.5 hours

marks.ride: the road and the clock appear, and a scooter sets off

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book about speed.
<bookmark mark='ride'/>{{NAME_9}} rides a hundred and twenty six kilometres from Pune to Matheran in two point five hours.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many kilometres does the scooter cover in one hour, on average?

beats.on_screen: the road, the clock and the empty speed meter stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: The words average speed = distance ÷ time; 2.5 = 25/10

marks.speed: the words average speed are written beside a one hour stretch of road
marks.rule: the rule distance divided by time is written

narration: <bookmark mark='speed'/>The distance covered in one hour is called the average speed.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>To find it, we divide the distance by the time.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>Two point five is the same as twenty five over ten, and that helps us divide.

marks.given: the distance and the time are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a distance of a hundred and twenty six kilometres, and a time of two point five hours.

beats.on_screen: To find: the average speed in km per hour
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the average speed in kilometres per hour.

marks.s1a: the rule average speed is distance divided by time is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, the average speed is the distance divided by the time.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>That is a hundred and twenty six divided by two point five.

marks.s2a: 2.5 is written as 25/10 inside the division
marks.s2b: the division by 25/10 is turned into a multiplication by 10/25

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, two point five is twenty five over ten.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Dividing by twenty five over ten is the same as multiplying by ten over twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>A hundred and twenty six times ten is one thousand two hundred and sixty. We get one thousand two hundred and sixty over twenty five.

beats.on_screen: 1260 ÷ 25 by long division: 1260 Ones ÷ 25 = 50 Ones, 10 Ones remain

marks.s3a: 1260 ÷ 25 is set in a long division frame
marks.s3b: fifty Ones go to the answer and ten Ones remain

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, a long division of one thousand two hundred and sixty by twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Divide the Ones by twenty five. That gives fifty Ones, and ten Ones remain.

beats.on_screen: decimal point placed; 10 Ones = 100 Tenths; 100 Tenths ÷ 25 = 4 Tenths; speed = 50 Ones + 4 Tenths = ?

marks.s4a: the point is placed and the ten Ones regroup into a hundred Tenths
marks.s4b: four Tenths go to the answer
marks.s4c: the speed is left blank beside fifty Ones and four Tenths

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, place the decimal point. Regroup the ten Ones into a hundred Tenths.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>A hundred Tenths divided by twenty five gives four Tenths.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>Put the shares together, fifty Ones and four Tenths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: average speed = 50.4 km per hour

marks.ans: 50.4 km per hour is boxed on the speed meter

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The average speed is fifty point four kilometres per hour.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the road
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 126 ÷ 25 = 5.04; a check 5.04 × 2.5 = 12.6 km is far short of 126 km; the bubble is crossed out and 126 becomes 1260

marks.fix: the scooter covers only 12.6 km on the road in 2.5 hours

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the speed is five point zero four kilometres per hour. That comes from changing two point five to twenty five and leaving the distance alone.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But at that speed, two point five hours cover only twelve point six kilometres. That is far less than a hundred and twenty six.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Change both numbers alike. Multiply the distance by ten too, and then use long division.
